subsection: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information
question_text: Why did the United States enter the Persian Gulf War?

official_answers.text: To force the Iraqi military from Kuwait

why_it_matters.text: On August 2, 1990, Iraq invaded its small oil-rich neighbor Kuwait. President George H.W. Bush assembled a 35-nation coalition under the United Nations to push Iraq out. After 5 weeks of air strikes and a brief ground war, Kuwait was liberated by February 28, 1991. About 148 Americans died in combat — far fewer than expected.

fun_fact.text: After 5 months of buildup, the Persian Gulf War ground assault began February 24, 1991. Just 100 hours later — about 4 days — President Bush declared victory. A 35-nation coalition had pushed Iraq out of Kuwait. The fastest decisive U.S. military victory of its scale in history. But Saddam Hussein stayed in power for 12 more years.
